scenario: A worker spends January and February outdoors for full shifts in temperatures that can reach minus 15 degrees Celsius. Their current phone can show about 40 percent charge and then shut down under use. They have a flexible budget up to $250 but do not want to buy a gimmick. They are comparing an OUKITEL WP9 rugged phone, a LATIMERIA 26800 mAh solar power bank, a compact TG90 6000 mAh wired power bank, and a JUBOTY 7000 mAh iPhone battery case. They need an evidence-bounded setup, an explanation of sudden cold shutdown, and a preflight that tests the actual phone, backup source, temperature, carrier, and work load before the setup is trusted for a full shift.

rules.complete_cold_shift_listing_matrix_v1: Audit the complete frozen product bodies rather than capacity labels alone. The OUKITEL WP9 body displays $219.99 and 67/100 over 12 reviews, claims an 8000 mAh battery, up to 48 hours of protection, an operating range of minus 10 to 70 degrees Celsius, IP68 and outdoor or skiing use, but restricts supported United States carriers and supplies seller claims rather than an independent minus 15 degree full-shift test. The LATIMERIA body displays $25.99 and 65/100 over 12 reviews, claims 26800 mAh, IPX4, dual USB output and a best operating range of minus 20 to 60 degrees Celsius, but explicitly says solar is only an emergency backup, recommends wall charging before travel, and supplies no independent full-shift test. The TG90 body displays $25.99 and 65/100 over 12 reviews, claims 6000 mAh, built-in cables and pocket size, but states no cold operating range or subfreezing load test. The JUBOTY body displays $20.83 and no reviews, claims 7000 mAh, but states a working range of 0 to 45 degrees Celsius and contains an internal mismatch between a 150 percent heading and a sentence that says 20 percent extra life. Preserve prices, review displays, temperature floors, carrier limits, seller attribution, and missing independent measurements.
rules.cold_shutdown_voltage_cutoff_scope_v1: A lithium-ion equivalent-circuit model separates open-circuit voltage from terminal voltage under load, includes resistance-related voltage drops, and says internal resistance increases significantly at low temperature. The cutoff-voltage page says phones automatically shut down at a lower voltage threshold and that a device can stop while significant capacity remains. Generic battery-management evidence says a system may monitor voltage, temperature, current, state of charge and state of power, and may stop operation for under-temperature conditions. Together these sources make a temporary low-temperature voltage and power limit a plausible explanation for a phone that displays charge and then shuts down, but they do not recover the exact true state of charge or diagnose this worker's phone without a matched measurement.
rules.winter_field_evidence_scope_v1: The soldier power-bank thread contains one commenter who reports two to three phone charges from a medium bank and at least one from a small bank during a really cold field exercise, plus other long-use Anker reports and warnings that small integrated solar panels provide little power. The commenter gives no temperature, phone model, bank model, rated capacity, measured energy, or controlled load, so the report is useful field experience rather than a transferable endurance test. A separate iPhone battery-pack thread distinguishes portable 10000 mAh packs from heavier 22000 to 23000 mAh packs and says one 26000 mAh Mophie supports multiple charges, but it is not a cold trial. A third thread contains conflicting claims after an owner attributes an iPhone screen failure to a random power bank; commenters dispute causation and warn that unknown brands may misstate protocols or capacity. These pages motivate portability, cable, brand, and safety checks but do not independently validate any frozen product for a minus 15 degree shift.
rules.insulation_and_cold_load_preflight_v1: Thermal insulation reduces heat transfer between objects at different temperatures, so an insulated inner pouch close to the body can delay cooling of both the phone and its backup source. This generic mechanism does not quantify how long a particular pouch keeps either battery inside its rated range. Before trusting a setup, verify carrier and connector compatibility, wall-charge the phone and backup, keep both together in the intended insulated inner location, reproduce the minus 15 degree environment and representative screen, radio, GPS, camera, and call load, record ambient and device temperature, displayed state of charge, loaded terminal behavior, shutdown or warning events, charge delivered, cable behavior, and recovery after warming, and repeat across a full shift. Do not use in-field solar input as the primary recharge plan, and stop if the device or pack is outside its stated operating range or reports a safety warning.
rules.evidence_bounded_cold_shift_decision_v1: For a shift that can reach minus 15 degrees Celsius, reject the JUBOTY route because its stated floor is 0 degrees and do not choose the TG90 route as the only backup because its frozen body gives no cold range. Do not replace the current phone with the OUKITEL solely for its 8000 mAh or rugged wording: its seller-stated floor is minus 10 degrees, warmer than the scenario minimum, its carrier support is restricted, and no independent full-shift test is present. The LATIMERIA is the only frozen backup candidate whose seller-stated range reaches minus 15 degrees, but its 26800 mAh, IPX4 and minus 20 degree wording remains unverified seller evidence and its own body says solar charging is emergency-only. The evidence-bounded default is therefore to keep the current phone, wall-charge the LATIMERIA as a wired backup, carry both warm in an insulated inner pouch, and trust the combination only after the prescribed minus 15 degree full-shift load test. If the actual workplace falls outside the product range, the carrier fails, or the trial fails, defer purchase or deployment and seek a separately verified cold-rated route. No frozen source proves a guaranteed full shift, an exact hidden charge percentage, or a universally safe power-bank brand.
